Let's build this properly. I'll give you the full blueprint for your AI QA Testing Assistant.

1. The Core Vision

Name idea: TestForge AI or QA Copilot

Tagline: Paste requirement -> Get test cases, edge cases, API tests, and Jira-ready bug reports.

2. The 6 Core Modules (Your MVP)

Here's how each feature you listed should work:

A. Requirement → Test Case Generator
Input: PRD text, user story, or Jira ticket description.
Output: Structured test cases in Gherkin / TestRail format.
Tech: LLM prompt + template: Requirement + Context + Output Format (Test Case ID, Title, Precondition, Steps, Expected Result, Priority)

B. Edge Case Detector
This is your secret weapon. Most AI tools miss this.
Prompt layer: "Act as a senior QA who loves breaking things. List: boundary values, null/empty, unicode, concurrency, auth bypass, rate limits, timezones, offline."
You add a rules engine on top of LLM: if field type = email -> auto-add invalid formats, if number -> -1, 0, MAX_INT.

C. User Story → Test Scenarios Converter
Input: "As a user, I want to login..."
Output: Happy path, alternative path, negative path.
Format: BDD Gherkin Given/When/Then — directly usable by automation teams.

D. Bug Report Creator
Input: "Login fails with 500 error when password has @ symbol"
Output: Professional bug report: Title, Severity, Priority, Steps to Reproduce, Expected vs Actual, Environment, Logs, Suggested labels. Ready to push to Jira.

E. API Test Suggester
Input: Swagger/OpenAPI URL or JSON payload.
Output: Postman collection with tests for status codes, schema validation, auth, negative tests.
Bonus: Auto-generate pm.test() assertions.

F. Regression Suite Builder
Input: Git diff / Recent commits / List of changed modules.
Output: "These 15 test cases are high-risk and must be in regression. These 40 can be skipped." Uses history + LLM reasoning.

3. Best Tech Stack for You (Portfolio-Ready)

You want it to look serious, but still buildable in 3-4 weeks:

Frontend: Next.js + Tailwind + shadcn/ui — Clean, developer-tool aesthetic
Backend: Python FastAPI (perfect for AI) or Node.js
AI Layer: OpenAI API / Claude API or local Llama 3 via Groq. Use function calling for structured JSON output.
Database: Supabase / Postgres — store test cases, history
Integrations:

  • Jira: Jira Cloud REST API + OAuth 2.0. Pull issue -> Generate tests -> Create sub-task.
  • Postman: Generate Postman Collection v2.1 JSON format. User can Import with 1 click.
  • GitHub: GitHub App + Webhooks. Listen to PRs -> Comment with suggested regression suite + generated tests.

Architecture:
User Input (Jira/Postman/GitHub) -> FastAPI -> Prompt Orchestrator -> LLM (with QA system prompts) -> Output Parser (JSON) -> Formatter (Gherkin / Postman JSON / Jira Markdown) -> Frontend + Integration Push

4. Build Roadmap - 4 Weeks

Week 1: Core Engine
Build the 6 prompts and get structured JSON output working. No UI. Just a CLI that takes requirements and prints test cases. This is 70% of the value.

Week 2: Web App
Build the Next.js UI: Left side = Input (tabs: Requirement / User Story / API Spec), Right side = Generated output with Copy / Export to CSV / Postman.

Week 3: Integrations

  1. Jira: "Connect Jira" button -> fetch ticket -> generate.
  2. Postman: Export button -> downloads .json collection.
  3. GitHub: Simple action — paste GitHub PR link -> analyze diff -> suggest regression.

Week 4: Polish & Launch
Add: Auth, history, Test case management dashboard, Landing page with demo video. Deploy to Vercel + Render. Write a great README with GIFs.

5. Prompt Template to Start With Today

Here's your first working prompt for test case generation:

You are a Senior QA Engineer with 10 years experience. Analyze the requirement below.

Requirement: {{requirement}}

Generate 8-12 test cases in JSON format: [{id, title, type:, priority:, precondition, steps[], expected_result, edge_case_rationale }]
Include at least 3 edge cases that junior testers would miss.[functional][boundary][negative][security][P0][P1][P2]

Force JSON mode in OpenAI to make it reliable.

Today
Show thinking

This is a classic Windows + Python issue — two problems, both easy to fix. Let's fix it in VSCode:

Problem 1: failed-wheel-build-for-install pydantic-core

Windows doesn't have the C++ tools to build Pydantic from source. Fix by forcing pre-built wheels.

Do this in VSCode Terminal (PowerShell):

Step A — Fix PowerShell execution so venv can activate:

powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser

Press Y then Enter. This is required on Windows, otherwise venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1 is blocked.

Step B — Delete old venv and recreate with Python 3.11:

powershell
# Close VSCode, reopen# Check Python version - must be 3.10 or 3.11, NOT 3.12 or 3.13 (causes wheel errors)python --version# If it's 3.12+, install Python 3.11 from python.org and use py -3.11
# Close VSCode, reopen# Check Python version - must be 3.10 or 3.11, NOT 3.12 or 3.13 (causes wheel errors)python --version# If it's 3.12+, install Python 3.11 from python.org and use py -3.11# Delete old venvRemove-Item -Recurse -Force venv# Create freshpython -m venv venv.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1# You should see (venv) at start of line now - very important!python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip

Step C — Install with wheels only (no building):

powershell
pip install --only-binary :all: fastapi uvicorn openai python-dotenv pydantic httpx# Now install the restpip install -r requirements.txt --only-binary :all:

If that still fails, use this Windows-safe requirements:

Create new file requirements-windows.txt in backend/ folder:

Code
fastapi==0.104.1uvicorn==0.24.0openai==1.12.0python-dotenv==1.0.0pydantic==2.5.0

Then:

powershell
pip install -r requirements-windows.txt

Problem 2: uvicorn not recognized

This means venv is NOT activated, or you're using uvicorn directly instead of python -m uvicorn.

Always run with python -m on Windows:

powershell
# Make sure you see (venv) in terminal!.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1# Use python -m, NOT just uvicornpython -m uvicorn main:app --reload --port 8000

If you still see (venv) missing, you didn't activate. Do:

powershell
# In backend folder.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1# Now runpython -m pip list# You should see fastapi, uvicorn in list

Full Working Sequence — Copy Paste This:

Open VSCode → Terminal → PowerShell → Run exactly:

powershell
cd backendRemove-Item -Recurse -Force venv -ErrorAction SilentlyContinuepython -m venv venv.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1python.exe -m pip install --upgrade pip setuptools wheel

You should see:

Code
INFO:     Uvicorn running on http://127.0.0.1:8000

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs — it works!

Why this happens on Windows:

  • pydantic-core is Rust-based and needs Visual C++ Build Tools to compile. Using --only-binary :all: tells pip "don't try to build, download the pre-built wheel"
  • PowerShell blocks script activation by default, so venv never activates, so uvicorn command not found. Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned fixes it.

Now — Let's Trace How Frontend Calls Backend (Open these 3 files in VSCode side-by-side):

1. backend/main.py — The Router (like a receptionist)

Python
@app.post("/api/generate-test-cases")async def generate_test_cases(data: RequirementInput):    result = await llm.generate_test_cases(data.requirement)    return result
  • @app.post means: "When frontend does fetch(POST to this URL), run this function"
  • RequirementInput is Pydantic — it validates: "Did frontend send requirement field? Is it a string?"
  • If frontend sends wrong data, FastAPI auto-returns error — you don't need to code validation

2. backend/services/llm_service.py — The Brain

Python
SYSTEM = "You are CaseForge AI, Senior QA..."PROMPTS["test_cases"] = "Generate 10-12 test cases..."async def _call(self, prompt):    if self.use_mock:  # No API key? Return mock
SYSTEM = "You are CaseForge AI, Senior QA..."PROMPTS["test_cases"] = "Generate 10-12 test cases..."async def _call(self, prompt):    if self.use_mock:  # No API key? Return mock        return self._mock(prompt)    else:  # Has key? Call real OpenAI        return await client.chat.completions.create(...)
  • use_mock check is why your app works even without paying OpenAI — perfect for demo
  • _mock() returns CF_001, CF_002 etc. — same shape as real AI, so frontend doesn't know difference

3. frontend/app/index.html — The Caller

Look for callApi function:

JavaScript
const apiUrl = localStorage.getItem('caseforge_api_url') // http://localhost:8000fetch(`${apiUrl}/api/generate-test-cases`, {  method: 'POST',  body: JSON.stringify({requirement: "Users reset password..."})})

This is the connection! Frontend sends JSON → Backend receives → Backend calls LLM → Returns JSON → Frontend renders cards.

That 404 means python -m http.server can't find the file — it's looking in the wrong folder. Super common first-time mistake.

Let's fix it for Windows VSCode:

Fix 1 — Check Where Your Files Actually Are

In VSCode terminal, run:

powershell
dir frontenddir frontend\app

You should see index.html or app.html inside. If you see nothing, you didn't save the downloaded files yet.

Do this:

-

📎 /mnt/data/testforge-landing_agentic_artifact_2_12b22558130d.html

→ Save to caseforge-ai\frontend\landing\index.html

  1. Verify:
powershell
cd caseforge-aidir frontend\app\index.htmldir frontend\landing\index.html

Both should show file size > 0.

Fix 2 — Run Server From The RIGHT Folder

http.server serves files from the folder you run it in. You must cd into that folder first.

powershell
# Close old server (Ctrl+C)# For APP:cd frontend\apppython -m http.server 3000
# Close old server (Ctrl+C)# For APP:cd frontend\apppython -m http.server 3000# Now open: http://localhost:3000/# NOT http://localhost:3000/app.html — just /# For LANDING (in new terminal):cd ..\landingpython -m http.server 3001# Open: http://localhost:3001/

Important: If file is named index.html, you open http://localhost:3000/ . If it's named app.html, you open http://localhost:3000/app.html — the name must match.

Easiest Fix — Use VSCode Live Server (No 404 ever)

This is better for beginners than python server:

  1. In VSCode, go to Extensions (Ctrl+Shift+X) → Search Live Server by Ritwick Dey → Install
  2. In Explorer, right-click on frontend\app\index.html → Open with Live Server

This is the same pydantic-core error but now on Render — not your fault. Render is using Python 3.14 (see log: /python3.14) which is too new, and it has no pre-built wheels for Pydantic, so it tries to build Rust and fails with Read-only file system.

Let's fix Render deploy in 2 minutes:

Fix — Tell Render to Use Python 3.11 (Not 3.14)

Method 1 — Easiest (Environment Variable):

  1. In Render dashboard → Your Web Service → Environment tab → Add Environment Variable

  2. Add:

Code
Key: PYTHON_VERSIONValue: 3.11.9
  1. Add second variable (forces binary only):
Code
Key: PIP_EXTRA_ARGSValue: --only-binary :all:
  1. Go to Settings → Scroll to Build & Deploy → Clear Build Cache & Deploy

It will now build with Python 3.11 which has wheels for Pydantic.

Method 2 — Create file in your repo (more reliable):

In VSCode, in backend/ folder, create file named .python-version (no extension):

Code
3.11.9

Also create runtime.txt in backend/:

Code
python-3.11.9

And replace your backend/requirements.txt with this Render-safe version (no Rust build needed):

Code
fastapi==0.104.1uvicorn==0.24.0pydantic==2.5.0python-dotenv==1.0.0httpx==0.25.0

Then push to GitHub:

powershell
cd caseforge-aigit add backend/.python-version backend/runtime.txt backend/requirements.txtgit commit -m "Fix Render Python version to 3.11"git push

Render auto-redeploys with Python 3.11.

Alternative — Even Simpler Build Command:

In Render → Settings → Build Command, change to:

Code
pip install --upgrade pip && pip install --only-binary :all: -r requirements.txt

This tells Render: "Don't try to build Rust, download wheels only"

Try Method 1 first (PYTHON_VERSION env var) — it's instant. Click Manual Deploy → Clear Build Cache & Deploy after adding it.

Idea A system that: - generates test cases from requirements - detects edge cases - creates bug reports - converts user stories into test scenarios - performs API test suggestions - creates regression suites Bonus Integrate with: - Jira - Postman - GitHub Why It’s Valuable Very few junior developers build tools for developers. Show thinking

This is exactly how you turn QA experience into a standout project. Recruiters see 100 todo-apps — almost no junior builds a tool for developers.

Let's build this properly. I'll give you the full blueprint for your AI QA Testing Assistant.

1. The Core Vision

Name idea: TestForge AI or QA Copilot

Tagline: Paste requirement -> Get test cases, edge cases, API tests, and Jira-ready bug reports.

2. The 6 Core Modules (Your MVP)

Here's how each feature you listed should work:

A. Requirement → Test Case Generator
Input: PRD text, user story, or Jira ticket description.
Output: Structured test cases in Gherkin / TestRail format.
Tech: LLM prompt + template: Requirement + Context + Output Format (Test Case ID, Title, Precondition, Steps, Expected Result, Priority)

B. Edge Case Detector
This is your secret weapon. Most AI tools miss this.
Prompt layer: "Act as a senior QA who loves breaking things. List: boundary values, null/empty, unicode, concurrency, auth bypass, rate limits, timezones, offline."
You add a rules engine on top of LLM: if field type = email -> auto-add invalid formats, if number -> -1, 0, MAX_INT.

C. User Story → Test Scenarios Converter
Input: "As a user, I want to login..."
Output: Happy path, alternative path, negative path.
Format: BDD Gherkin Given/When/Then — directly usable by automation teams.

D. Bug Report Creator
Input: "Login fails with 500 error when password has @ symbol"
Output: Professional bug report: Title, Severity, Priority, Steps to Reproduce, Expected vs Actual, Environment, Logs, Suggested labels. Ready to push to Jira.

E. API Test Suggester
Input: Swagger/OpenAPI URL or JSON payload.
Output: Postman collection with tests for status codes, schema validation, auth, negative tests.
Bonus: Auto-generate pm.test() assertions.

F. Regression Suite Builder
Input: Git diff / Recent commits / List of changed modules.
Output: "These 15 test cases are high-risk and must be in regression. These 40 can be skipped." Uses history + LLM reasoning.

3. Best Tech Stack for You (Portfolio-Ready)

You want it to look serious, but still buildable in 3-4 weeks:

Frontend: Next.js + Tailwind + shadcn/ui — Clean, developer-tool aesthetic
Backend: Python FastAPI (perfect for AI) or Node.js
AI Layer: OpenAI API / Claude API or local Llama 3 via Groq. Use function calling for structured JSON output.
Database: Supabase / Postgres — store test cases, history
Integrations:

  • Jira: Jira Cloud REST API + OAuth 2.0. Pull issue -> Generate tests -> Create sub-task.
  • Postman: Generate Postman Collection v2.1 JSON format. User can Import with 1 click.
  • GitHub: GitHub App + Webhooks. Listen to PRs -> Comment with suggested regression suite + generated tests.

Architecture:
User Input (Jira/Postman/GitHub) -> FastAPI -> Prompt Orchestrator -> LLM (with QA system prompts) -> Output Parser (JSON) -> Formatter (Gherkin / Postman JSON / Jira Markdown) -> Frontend + Integration Push

4. Build Roadmap - 4 Weeks

Week 1: Core Engine
Build the 6 prompts and get structured JSON output working. No UI. Just a CLI that takes requirements and prints test cases. This is 70% of the value.

Week 2: Web App
Build the Next.js UI: Left side = Input (tabs: Requirement / User Story / API Spec), Right side = Generated output with Copy / Export to CSV / Postman.

Week 3: Integrations

  1. Jira: "Connect Jira" button -> fetch ticket -> generate.
  2. Postman: Export button -> downloads .json collection.
  3. GitHub: Simple action — paste GitHub PR link -> analyze diff -> suggest regression.

Week 4: Polish & Launch
Add: Auth, history, Test case management dashboard, Landing page with demo video. Deploy to Vercel + Render. Write a great README with GIFs.

5. Prompt Template to Start With Today

Here's your first working prompt for test case generation:

You are a Senior QA Engineer with 10 years experience. Analyze the requirement below.

Requirement: {{requirement}}

Generate 8-12 test cases in JSON format: [{id, title, type:, priority:, precondition, steps[], expected_result, edge_case_rationale }]
Include at least 3 edge cases that junior testers would miss.[functional][boundary][negative][security][P0][P1][P2]

Force JSON mode in OpenAI to make it reliable.

6. How This Gets You Hired

Don't just put it on GitHub. Do this:

  1. Demo video: Show Jira ticket -> 1 click -> Full test suite in Jira.
  2. Live link: testforge.yourname.dev
  3. README: Architecture diagram, integrations, example inputs/outputs.
  4. LinkedIn Post: "I built a tool that converts Jira tickets to Postman collections using AI. Here's how..."

This proves you understand: QA, Developer Workflow, AI, and API integrations — four skills in one project.
